parsed.answer: The evidence identifies pyridostatin (PDS) as a G4-stabilizing compound and states that G4-forming genomic sequences include telomeres; PDS treatment increases telomere fragility in BRCA2-deficient cells, which the authors attribute to G4 formation driving telomere instability. Thus PDS is described as stabilizing G-quadruplexes in the context of telomeric G-rich repeats, though the excerpt asserts the telomere-level effect indirectly via fragility rather than a direct biophysical measurement of stabilization at telomeres.
